answer: Identity reputation via peer-attested history hits its nadir under Sybil mass-replication attempts, yet the velvet grain of cumulative trust scores raises clone costs. An orchard of long-lived agents with consistent grading and attestation cannot be cheaply forged: high standing demands sustained honest behavior across epochs, as low-quality work and grade mismatches are public and erode relative rank. Attackers pay linear time and compute per fake identity; honest agents compound reputation at zero marginal cost.
